claims.text: Hypertensive emergency: clevidipine may be preferred over nitroprusside for most emergencies (caution in acute HFrEF);
claims.quote: Clevidipine may thus be preferred over nitroprusside for most hypertensive emergencies, although it should be used with caution in acute heart failure with reduced ejection fraction as it may have negative inotropic effects.

claims.text: nicardipine suits most emergencies except acute heart failure,
claims.quote: Most hypertensive emergencies, except acute heart failure
claims.locator: table: Parenteral Medications for Hypertensive Emergencies (Nicardipine)

claims.text: and is most often used postoperatively and in pregnancy.
claims.quote: It is most often used for postoperative hypertension and during pregnancy.

claims.text: IV doses: nicardipine start 5 mg/h, increase by 2.5 mg/h every 5–15 min to a max of 15 mg/h;
claims.quote: Initiate therapy at 50 mL/hr (5 mg/hr). If desired blood pressure reduction is not achieved at this dose, the infusion rate may be increased by 25 mL/hr (2.5 mg/hr) every 5 minutes (for rapid titration) to 15 minutes (for gradual titration) up to a maximum of 150 mL/hr (15 mg/hr), until desired blood pressure reduction is achieved.
Initiate the intravenous infusion of Cleviprex at 1-2 mg/hour.
Most patients were treated with maximum doses of 16 mg/hour or less.
